original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-closed-immersion-almost-full}
Let $i : Z \to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes.
Let $U, U'$ be schemes \'etale over $X$. Let $h : U_Z \to U'_Z$
be a morphism over $Z$. Then there exists a diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
U & W \ar[l]_a \ar[r]^b & U'
}
$$
in $X_\etale$ such that $a_Z : W_Z \to U_Z$
is an isomorphism and $h = b_Z \circ (a_Z)^{-1}$.

final_content.statement:
Let $X_{\acute et}$ and $Y_{\acute et}$ denote the **small étale sites** of schemes $X$ and $Y$, and let $\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute et})$ be the corresponding topoi of sheaves of sets, with structure sheaves of local rings $\mathcal O_X,\mathcal O_Y$ on these sites. A scheme map $f:X\to Y$ induces a geometric morphism $f_{\mathrm{small}}:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute et})\to\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\acute et})$ with inverse-image functor $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}$ (left adjoint to direct image $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$) and a ring map $f_{\mathrm{small}}^\sharp:f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$. A *morphism of locally ringed topoi* is a geometric morphism together with a structure-ring map inducing **local homomorphisms on all stalks**, not merely a morphism of ringed topoi. A *2-morphism* between two such morphisms is a natural transformation of inverse-image functors compatible with their structure sheaf maps; a 2-isomorphism is an invertible 2-morphism. The morphism $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$ on abelian sheaves is the direct-image right adjoint.

For $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$, $(\mathrm{Sch}/X)_\tau$ and $(\mathrm{Sch}/Y)_\tau$ denote the **big** $\tau$-sites (small-universe selections of schemes over the bases). A scheme map $f:X\to Y$ induces $f_{\mathrm{big}}:\operatorname{Sh}((\mathrm{Sch}/X)_\tau)\to\operatorname{Sh}((\mathrm{Sch}/Y)_\tau)$ with inverse image and direct image adjoints. A *monomorphism of schemes* is a morphism $f$ with injective functor-of-points maps $T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(T,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,Y)$ for every scheme $T$. A *closed immersion* realizes $X$ as a closed subscheme of $Y$; its étale base changes remain closed immersions. A site functor is **almost cocontinuous** when pullbacks of covering families are locally refinable by covering families whose pieces either map into a source cover member or map to the empty scheme; this is the weaker lifting criterion used for big-site direct image exactness.

Let $U, U'$ be schemes \'etale over $X$. Let $h : U_Z \to U'_Z$
be a morphism over $Z$. Then there exists a diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
U & W \ar[l]_a \ar[r]^b & U'
}
$$

\label{lemma-closed-immersion-almost-essentially-surjective}
Let $i : Z \to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes.
Let $V \to Z$ be an \'etale morphism of schemes.
There exist \'etale morphisms $U_i \to X$ and morphisms
$U_{i, Z} \to V$ such that $\{U_{i, Z} \to V\}$
is a Zariski covering of $V$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-stalk-pushforward-closed-immersion}
Let $i : Z \to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a sheaf of sets on $Z_\etale$.
Let $\overline{x}$ be a geometric point of $X$.
Then
$$
(i_{small, *}\mathcal{G})_{\overline{x}} =
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
* & \text{if} & \overline{x} \not \in Z \\
\mathcal{G}_{\overline{x}} & \text{if} & \overline{x} \in Z
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$
where $*$ denotes a singleton set.
